## DummyInternalMethodHandler

```java
public class DummyInternalMethodHandler implements IInternalMethodHandler
```

The original inert fallback handler: every call succeeds silently or reports "nothing known".

The native port installs a real handler in `ThaumcraftApi.internalMethods`; this class stays available so that an add-on can restore the inert behaviour deliberately.

<a id="dummyinternalmethodhandler-generateviseffect"></a>
```java
public void generateVisEffect(int dim, int x, int y, int z, int x2, int y2, int z2, int color)
```

> **Deprecated.**

Does nothing; dimension is a legacy numeric ID, endpoints are block coordinates and color is RGB.

**Deprecated:** Use VisNetHandler.generateVisEffect with ServerLevel, BlockPos endpoints and Aspect for a real effect.

## IInternalMethodHandler

```java
public interface IInternalMethodHandler
```

The original TC4 plug point that lets the API reach the gameplay internals it must not own.

The original declares one interface with two implementations: the real `thaumcraft.common.lib.InternalMethodHandler` and the dummy `thaumcraft.api.internal.DummyInternalMethodHandler`. Both are ported; the interface therefore carries the original method set *and* the 1.21.1 forms of the same services, so an add-on must adapt 1.7.10 Minecraft types to 1.21.1 types; this is not source or binary compatibility.

The defaults are inert so that a replacement handler written for 1.7.10 still compiles; the installed ThaumcraftInternalMethods implements every service of this interface except the numeric-dimension effect, which has no 1.21.1 meaning.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-generateviseffect"></a>
```java
default void generateVisEffect(ServerLevel level, int x, int y, int z, int x2, int y2, int z2, int color)
```

The original vis drain effect between two block positions of a server level; color is RGB. Does nothing by default; the installed handler sends the original effect packet. The 1.21.1 form of the numeric-dimension overload below.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-isresearchcomplete"></a>
```java
default boolean isResearchComplete(Player player, String researchKey)
```

Player-scoped service. Old addon handlers retain their username override through this default.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-hasdiscoveredaspect"></a>
```java
default boolean hasDiscoveredAspect(Player player, Aspect aspect)
```

Player-scoped form of `Aspect)`; false by default and for null arguments. The installed handler reads the player's own knowledge, on either side.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-getdiscoveredaspects"></a>
```java
default AspectList getDiscoveredAspects(Player player)
```

Player-scoped form of `getDiscoveredAspects(String)`: a new list of the discovered aspects and their pools; null by default and for a null player.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-getstackinrowandcolumn"></a>
```java
default ItemStack getStackInRowAndColumn(Object instance, int row, int column)
```

Returns EMPTY by default, including null instance; row/column are zero-based 3x3 grid indices, not block coordinates.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-getobjectaspects"></a>
```java
default AspectList getObjectAspects(Level level, ItemStack stack)
```

World-scoped base aspects of a stack (registered, recipe-derived and inferred), as a new list; null by default. The installed handler needs a loaded server recipe context for recipe-derived tags.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-getbonusobjecttags"></a>
```java
default AspectList getBonusObjectTags(Level level, ItemStack stack, AspectList bonus)
```

World-scoped full aspects of a stack (equipment, enchantments, contents) plus `bonus`, as a new list; null by default.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-generatetags"></a>
```java
default AspectList generateTags(Level level, Item item, int metadata)
```

World-scoped recipe-derived aspects of an item, as a new list; null by default. metadata is native damage points, not old subtype metadata.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-consumevisfromwand"></a>
```java
default boolean consumeVisFromWand(ItemStack wand, Player player, AspectList cost, boolean doit, boolean crafting)
```

Returns false by default without reading nullable inputs or debiting vis; installed handlers define their own cost units/discount policy.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-consumevisfromwandcrafting"></a>
```java
default boolean consumeVisFromWandCrafting(ItemStack wand, Player player, AspectList cost, boolean doit)
```

Returns false by default without reading nullable inputs or changing stacks; installed handlers define cost conversion and payment semantics.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-consumevisfrominventory"></a>
```java
default boolean consumeVisFromInventory(Player player, AspectList cost)
```

Returns false by default without reading nullable inputs or changing inventory; installed handlers own payment behavior.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-completeresearch"></a>
```java
default boolean completeResearch(Player player, String researchKey)
```

Original `ResearchManager.completeResearch(player, key)`: completes the research, its parents and siblings as the original did, pays its warp and syncs the player. Server side only; false by default, on a client, for an unknown or disabled key.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-getcompletedresearch"></a>
```java
default java.util.Set<String> getCompletedResearch(Player player)
```

The research keys a player completed, as a new set without the "@" clue markers; empty by default and for null.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-addaspectpool"></a>
```java
default void addAspectPool(Player player, Aspect aspect, int amount)
```

Original `ResearchManager.completeAspect`: adds research points of an aspect to the player's pool (the points the research table spends) and syncs. Server side only; no-op by default. amount is clamped to a short.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-getaspectpool"></a>
```java
default int getAspectPool(Player player, Aspect aspect)
```

The research points of an aspect in the player's pool; zero by default and for null arguments.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-getwarp"></a>
```java
default int[] getWarp(Player player)
```

The permanent, sticky and temporary warp of a player, in that order, as a new three-element array; zeros by default.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-addwarptoplayer"></a>
```java
default void addWarpToPlayer(Player player, int amount, boolean temporary)
```

Default no-op, ignoring nullable player, signed warp-point amount and temporary flag; sends no packet.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-addstickywarptoplayer"></a>
```java
default void addStickyWarpToPlayer(Player player, int amount)
```

Default no-op, ignoring nullable player and signed warp-point amount; sends no packet.

<a id="iinternalmethodhandler-generateviseffect-3"></a>
```java
default void generateVisEffect(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos from, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos to, thaumcraft.api.aspects.Aspect aspect)
```

The vis drain effect from a node to its consumer for one aspect; does nothing by default, on a client level and for null arguments. The installed handler forwards to VisNetHandler.generateVisEffect(ServerLevel, BlockPos, BlockPos, Aspect).

## ThaumcraftInternalMethods

```java
public final class ThaumcraftInternalMethods implements IInternalMethodHandler
```

The native handler bound to the 1.21.1 gameplay internals.

Everything the original `DummyInternalMethodHandler` refused to answer is answered here from the live native state: the player's own knowledge, the native object-tag registry, the native wand payment and the native warp bookkeeping. Nothing is cached across a player or world change; the server reference used to resolve a player name is weak and follows the native server lifecycle.

```java
public ThaumcraftInternalMethods()
public static void serverStarted(MinecraftServer server)
public static void serverStopped(MinecraftServer server)
```

<a id="thaumcraftinternalmethods-getstackinrowandcolumn"></a>
```java
public ItemStack getStackInRowAndColumn(Object instance, int row, int column)
```

The original three by three grid lookup.

Original `thaumcraft/common/lib/InternalMethodHandler.java` forwards to `TileMagicWorkbench.getStackInRowAndColumn(row, column)`, which reads the slot `row + column * 3` of the grid (oracle `TileMagicWorkbench.getStackInRowAndColumn`). The original recipes call the helper with the ROW first, for example `getStackInRowAndColumn(inv, 1, 0)` for the slot 1 of the sceptre grid (oracle `thaumcraft/common/lib/crafting/ArcaneSceptreRecipe.java:42-46`).
